message:
fix(update): check the owner, not the destination, and send the whole descriptor

Four defects, all of them in the gap between "each piece is right" and "the
chain runs".

The owner check was a url comparison. Same url, same origin, and a token
that is not empty -- which asks whether the SERVER changed. Sign out and
back in on the same server and all three still hold while the token is a
different one, so an attempt authorised by one sign-in would be handed the
credential of the next. The endpoint now carries an owner key and an epoch,
and both are compared: the key alone cannot see a re-login by the same
account, and the epoch alone cannot see a different account.

The credential travelled alone and the receiver rebuilt the origin from its
command line. So the value arrived over a channel that had proved who was
listening, and the origin it would be sent to arrived in argv, which had
proved nothing -- anything able to start the worker with a different
--manifest-url could aim a real credential elsewhere. Url, origin, owner,
epoch, wire shape and credential now travel in one frame, and the worker
checks the frame against its arguments. An unknown field is refused rather
than ignored: the two ends disagreeing about what the frame is, and guessing
which parts still apply, is how that disagreement gets buried.

Nothing checked the owner before the acknowledgement. "The owner was right
at launch" and "the owner is right now" are different statements and a
download takes minutes. await_handoff asks once, immediately before
acknowledging, and withholding it leaves the updater unable to stop
anything -- that is the last point where this can still be refused. The
client therefore joins a handshake it used to skip: having nothing to
withhold was only true while it had no credential to hand over.

And the 120-second wait sat inline in the page-message handler, so the
window stopped answering for up to two minutes. Overlapped I/O does not help
when the caller waits on the thread that has to paint. It runs on its own
thread now, owning the process handle and the pipe, and a credential that
was not delivered is reported as a failure rather than as "the update
started" -- the updater will run and install nothing, so saying it began
leaves the user waiting for a result that is not coming.
